about: Generated release 0 of the Tribes of Behavior atlas (ADR-0003 §10). Hand-authored before the database existed; import_atlas loads it as release 0, after which the database is the truth and export_atlas regenerates these files. Do not hand-edit after import.

tribes.name: Basque (Euskara)
tribes.note: A pre-Indo-European language isolate of the western Pyrenees.

tribes.name: Iberian & Tartessian
tribes.note: Non-Indo-European tongues of Iberia's east and south coasts, written in their own scripts.

tribes.name: Celtic, Celtiberian & Lusitanian
tribes.note: Celtic and related Indo-European tongues of ancient western Europe.

tribes.name: Phoenician / Punic
tribes.note: The Phoenician language and its Carthaginian (Punic) form, carried along the Mediterranean by traders.

tribes.name: Latin → Hispanic Romance
tribes.note: The language of Rome, ancestor of the Romance tongues.

tribes.name: Andalusi Romance (Mozarabic)
tribes.note: The Romance speech of al-Andalus.

tribes.name: Arabic
tribes.note: A Semitic language carried out of Arabia with Islam; the language of the Qur'an.

tribes.name: Tamazight (Berber)
tribes.note: The Amazigh (Berber) languages of North Africa and the Sahara.

tribes.name: Castilian (Spanish)
tribes.note: Spanish: a Romance tongue from Castile, now spoken on four continents.

tribes.name: Galician-Portuguese
tribes.note: Galician and Portuguese, from one medieval Romance tongue of Iberia's northwest.

tribes.name: Catalan
tribes.note: A Romance tongue of the western Mediterranean coast and islands.

tribes.name: Astur-Leonese
tribes.note: The Romance of the old kingdom of Asturias and León.

tribes.name: Navarro-Aragonese
tribes.note: The Romance of Navarre and Aragon.

tribes.name: Judeo-Spanish (Ladino, Haketia)
tribes.note: The Spanish of the Sephardic Jews, kept in exile after 1492.

tribes.name: Occitan & Gascon
tribes.note: The Romance tongue of southern France, language of the troubadours.

tribes.name: French
tribes.note: The Romance tongue of northern France, later a language of state and empire.

tribes.name: Indigenous cults (Iberian, Celtic, Vasconic)
tribes.note: Local cults of the ancient western Mediterranean and Atlantic peoples.

tribes.name: Phoenician & Punic cults
tribes.note: The gods of Tyre and Carthage — Melqart, Tanit, Baal Hammon.

tribes.name: Greek cults (Emporion)
tribes.note: The cults of the Greek colonies.

tribes.name: Roman civic & imperial cult
tribes.note: The public religion of Roman cities: the Capitoline gods and the emperor.

tribes.name: Judaism
tribes.note: The religion of the Jewish people.

tribes.name: Converso & crypto-Jewish
tribes.note: Jews baptised under pressure, and their descendants watched by the Inquisition.

tribes.name: Arian Christianity (Visigoths)
tribes.note: The Christianity of the Goths, denying Christ's equality with the Father.

tribes.name: Nicene / Catholic Christianity
tribes.note: Nicene, later Roman Catholic, Christianity.

tribes.name: Islam
tribes.note: The religion founded by Muhammad in seventh-century Arabia.

tribes.name: Unaffiliated & secular
tribes.note: No religious affiliation, or open unbelief.

tribes.name: Dry farming — wheat, olive, vine
tribes.note: Rain-fed farming of the Mediterranean triad: wheat, olive, vine.

tribes.name: Transhumant herding (the Mesta)
tribes.note: Moving flocks between summer and winter pastures.

tribes.name: Irrigated huerta — acequia & noria
tribes.note: Farming on canals, wells and waterwheels.

tribes.name: Mining
tribes.note: Digging metal and coal.

tribes.name: Seafaring, fishing & whaling
tribes.note: Living from the sea: fishing, whaling, shipping.

tribes.name: Silk & textiles
tribes.note: Spinning and weaving silk and other cloth for sale.

tribes.name: Heavy industry
tribes.note: Factory and furnace work.

tribes.name: Tourism & services
tribes.note: Tourism, offices and other service work.

tribes.name: Carthage
tribes.note: The empire of Carthage.

tribes.name: Roman Republic & Empire
tribes.note: Rule by the Roman Republic and Empire.

tribes.name: Suebic kingdom
tribes.note: The Germanic kingdom of the Suebi in Gallaecia.

tribes.name: Visigothic kingdom
tribes.note: The Visigothic kingdom, from Toulouse and then Toledo.

tribes.name: Byzantine (Eastern Roman) Empire
tribes.note: The Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire.

tribes.name: Umayyad al-Andalus
tribes.note: The Umayyad emirate and caliphate of Córdoba.

tribes.name: Taifas, Almoravids & Almohads
tribes.note: The taifa kingdoms and the Almoravid and Almohad empires.

tribes.name: Nasrid Granada
tribes.note: The Nasrid emirate of Granada.

tribes.name: Asturias → León → Castile
tribes.note: The kingdoms of Asturias, León and Castile.

tribes.name: Navarre
tribes.note: The kingdom of Navarre.

tribes.name: Barcelona → Crown of Aragon
tribes.note: The county of Barcelona and the Crown of Aragon.

tribes.name: Portugal
tribes.note: The kingdom, empire and republic of Portugal.

tribes.name: Spain
tribes.note: The Spanish monarchy and state, from 1479.

tribes.name: France
tribes.note: The French kingdom and republic.

tribes.name: Moroccan sultanates
tribes.note: The sultanates of Morocco.

tribes.name: African Romance
tribes.note: The Latin of Roman Africa, spoken on into the Islamic centuries.

tribes.name: Judeo-Arabic
tribes.note: The Arabic of Jewish communities, written in Hebrew letters.

tribes.name: Donatist Christianity
tribes.note: A North African church of the martyrs that refused bishops who had lapsed under persecution.

tribes.name: Kharijite & Ibadi Islam
tribes.note: Islam's first dissenters: any righteous believer may lead, even a slave. The Ibadi branch survives.

tribes.name: Isma'ili Shi'ism
tribes.note: The Shi'ism of the Fatimid caliphs.

tribes.name: Caravan trade — salt, gold, slaves
tribes.note: Long-distance trade by camel across the Sahara.

tribes.name: Corsairing
tribes.note: Privateering as a state industry: ships seized and captives ransomed or sold.

tribes.name: Oil & gas
tribes.note: Pumping hydrocarbons for export.

tribes.name: Numidia & Mauretania
tribes.note: The Berber kingdoms between Carthage and Rome.

tribes.name: Vandal kingdom
tribes.note: A Germanic kingdom ruled from Carthage, 439–534.

tribes.name: Umayyad & Abbasid caliphates
tribes.note: Rule from Damascus, then Baghdad.

tribes.name: Rustamid imamate
tribes.note: An Ibadi state ruled from Tahert, 777–909.

tribes.name: Idrisid Morocco
tribes.note: The first Muslim dynasty of Morocco, founders of Fez.

tribes.name: Aghlabid emirate
tribes.note: Abbasid governors who ruled Ifriqiya and conquered Sicily.

tribes.name: Fatimids & Zirids
tribes.note: An Isma'ili caliphate founded in Ifriqiya that moved to Cairo, and the Zirids who ruled behind it.

tribes.name: Hafsid Ifriqiya
tribes.note: The dynasty of Tunis, 1229–1574.

tribes.name: Zayyanid Tlemcen
tribes.note: The kingdom of Tlemcen, 1235–1556.

tribes.name: Ottoman regencies
tribes.note: Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli under the Ottoman sultan.

tribes.name: Algeria
tribes.note: The Algerian republic, from 1962.

tribes.name: Tunisia
tribes.note: The Tunisian republic, from 1956.

tribes.name: Scribal writing — clay, papyrus, bamboo
tribes.note: Reading and writing as the craft of a few: scribes, priests, clerks.

tribes.name: Manuscript culture — codex & paper
tribes.note: Books copied by hand and read aloud; paper from China, through Samarkand and Baghdad, to the Mediterranean.

tribes.name: Woodblock printing
tribes.note: Whole pages carved and printed — East Asia's print for a thousand years.

tribes.name: Printing press
tribes.note: Movable type in a press: identical books by the thousand.

tribes.name: Newspapers & mass literacy
tribes.note: Most people reading, and reading the same news on the same day.

tribes.name: Telegraph & post office
tribes.note: Words faster than any rider — the first signal that outran a body.

tribes.name: Radio
tribes.note: One voice heard by millions at once, no literacy required.

tribes.name: Television
tribes.note: Moving pictures in the home.

tribes.name: Internet
tribes.note: Everyone a publisher; distance stops being the measure of reach.

tribes.name: Mobile phone
tribes.note: The network in a pocket — in much of Africa and Asia, the first phone and the first screen.
